title: Replenish line-side bins by a min/max rule
instruction: replenish the line-side bins by their min/max rule: refill any bin holding fewer than 2 parts up to 3 parts from the bulk tote, and leave bins holding 2 or more alone
context: Line-side bins are replenished on min/max rules: a bin that has fallen below its minimum is topped up to its maximum, and full bins are left alone; overfilling wastes space and ties up stock, and missing a low bin starves the line. It measures counting and applying a threshold rule, rather than moving every part available.
setup: The table top is 74.75 cm above the floor. Two arms 61 cm apart on a table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. Three blue line-side bins (each inside 9 x 9 cm, 1 cm walls 3 cm tall, open-bottomed on the bench) are fixed at (33, 14), (33, 0) and (33, -14). Steel 3/4-inch drive sockets (NVIDIA SimReady model Socket_3_4in_A01: 3.0 cm across, 4.7 cm tall, 90 g) stand upright in them: one in the left bin, three in the middle bin, none in the right bin. A dark bulk tote (inside 6 x 30 cm, 1 cm walls 2 cm tall, open-bottomed) at (17, 0) holds six more sockets, in a row along y at y = -12.5, -7.5, -2.5, 2.5, 7.5 and 12.5.
scoring: A bin's count is the number of sockets whose centre is inside its walls, with their underside no more than 4 cm above the bin's floor. The left bin (1, below the minimum of 2) needs 2 more and the right bin (0) needs 3; the middle bin (3) needs none. Correct: sockets added to the left and right bins, up to those numbers. Wrong: sockets beyond 3 in any bin, and every socket taken out of any bin (a bin ending with fewer than it started with). Score = (correct - 1.5 x wrong) / 5, but not below 0. Doing nothing scores 0; one socket into each bin scores 0.1; 1.0 when every bin holds 3. Items are judged only by the positions stated above, not by how they are oriented, so one lying on its side counts the same as one standing; anything the rules above don't cover (for example a part dropped off the table) counts neither way unless a penalty above applies to it. On real arms, count the sockets in each bin from a top-down photo of the end state.
reset_notes: Put the added sockets back in the bulk tote so the bins hold 1, 3 and 0.
fidelity: Approximate. The sockets are NVIDIA SimReady models at real size; the bins and tote are fixed boxes, and the min/max levels are stated in the instruction rather than on bin labels. The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Friction is higher than for steel sockets on plastic bins, so sockets slip less in the grip than on real arms.
